judged_text: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters every credential's calendar list against mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId — the first destination calendar — on every create call, regardless of which host's credential is in use. For multi-destination collective events, a secondary host's CalDAV/Apple credential contains none of the first host's calendar URLs, so the filter yields an empty calendar list and no event is created on that host's calendar at all — the collective multi-host fix silently no-ops for every non-first CalDAV host.

For multi-destination collective events, a secondary host's CalDAV/Apple credential contains none of the first host's calendar URLs, so the filter yields an empty calendar list and no event is created on that host's calendar at all — the collective multi-host fix silently no-ops for every non-first CalDAV host.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (`BaseCalendarService.createEvent`), the code now derives `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and filters the credential’s `calendars` list by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (i.e., the *first* destination calendar) before creating the event. For collective/multi-destination events, `evt.destinationCalendar` is built as an array (organizer first, then other hosts via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` in `handleNewBooking.ts`). When `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterates destinations/credentials, a non-first host’s CalDAV/Apple credential will list calendars that do not include the first host’s calendar URL, so this filter can yield an empty set and no event is created for that host. The diff shows no mechanism in `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` to select the destination calendar matching the current credential, so the finding is directly grounded.
